title: Replication Assay
description: Assign parasites to vacuoles, inspect the one-two-four-eight replication ladder, and compare intracellular replication between conditions with vacuole- and well-level QC.
objectives: Choose a defensible vacuole assignment method and avoid treating host-cell identity as vacuole identity.
Audit parasite and vacuole filters, replication buckets, condition metadata, and non-power-of-two QC.
Interpret parasites-per-vacuole distributions and condition comparisons without pseudoreplication.
prerequisite: Measure one row per segmented parasite with plate, well, field, host-cell, and—ideally—independently validated vacuole identifiers.

scenes.narration: Assay Inputs identifies the experiment root, one-row-per-parasite table, and pathogen compartment. Replication scores existing parasite measurements; it does not segment microscopy images again.

scenes.narration: Vacuole Assignment first uses an explicit vacuole key when present, otherwise it can link parasite centroids spatially, and only then fall back to host-cell grouping. A host cell may contain multiple vacuoles, so that fallback can merge biologically distinct units.

scenes.narration: Condition Metadata maps plate wells to biological groups and chooses the comparison column. This synthetic plate contains six vehicle wells in column one and six inhibitor wells in column two, all with HeLa host cells.

scenes.narration: Object Filtering rejects pathogen measurements outside the accepted area range before vacuoles are counted. These limits must be validated against segmented parasites, because debris and merged objects distort the replication ladder in opposite directions.
scenes.speech_text: Object Filtering rejects pathogen measurements outside the accepted area range before vacuoles are counted. These limits must be validated against segmented parasites, because debris and merged objects distort the replication ladder in opposite directions.

scenes.narration: Replication Scoring defines the largest named count bucket and the warning threshold for non-power-of-two vacuoles. Counts one, two, four, eight, and sixteen follow ideal doubling; counts such as three are retained as a QC category rather than silently rounded.

scenes.narration: This assignment detail uses the explicit vacuole_id column and requires a host cell. The synthetic data intentionally gives some consecutive vacuoles the same cell ID, confirming that the chosen vacuole key—not the host cell—is the unit being counted.

scenes.narration: Click Run after checking inputs, assignment, condition metadata, filters, and scoring. The backend groups parasites into vacuoles, labels count buckets, summarizes wells and conditions, performs pairwise tests, and renders the distributions.

scenes.narration: During execution, the console exposes the selected tables and comparison method. Inspect vacuoles at low and high counts in their source images before treating a distribution shift as biology rather than segmentation or assignment error.

scenes.narration: The real backend scores two hundred forty vacuoles in each condition. Vehicle has median four parasites and two doublings per vacuole; inhibitor has median two parasites and one doubling. Both groups contain five percent non-power-of-two vacuoles and remain below the twenty-percent warning. With six wells per group, the displayed Mann–Whitney comparison is strongly separated, but biological conclusions still require independent experiments.
